title: quercus lanuginosa var. parviglandis
intro: Quercus lanuginosa var. parviglandis, commonly known as Japanese oak, is a plant species in the beech family (Fagaceae). It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to protect against chronic diseases such as cancer and heart disease. The therapeutic actions of this plant include its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce oxidative stress, and exhibit antimicrobial activities. The bioactive constituents of Quercus lanuginosa var. parviglandis include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other polyphenolic compounds that contribute to its medicinal properties.
